metadata.title: MARKETS LIVE: Wall Street rallies in early trading

content.text:
-
Dow Jones up 211.32 points at 50,409.49
-
Nasdaq up 494.88 points at 24,924.77
-
S&P 500 up 89.33 points at 7,412.85
9.30 EST: Nasdaq jumps nearly 495 points
The Dow Jones and S&P 500 rose in early trading on Thursday, with the Nasdaq leading gains ahead of Anthropic's expected market debut.
Temu owner PDD Holdings led the gainers, rising 8.76% to $84.24 after its third-quarter adjusted profit beat Wall Street expectations.
Campbell's led the fallers, sliding 5.66% to $22.99.
8.00 EST: Nasdaq 100 futures jump 560 points after record IPO pricing
Dow Jones, Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 rose on Thursday ahead of the Wall Street open after Anthropic priced its initial public offering above expectations, reviving demand for artificial intelligence stocks.
The maker of Claude is due to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday after pricing its record $81.34 billion offering at $83 a share. The price values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
Nvidia was up 1.5%, and Advanced Micro Devices gained 2.9%. Micron Technology climbed 4.8%, while SK Hynix's American depositary receipts rose 5.3%. Intel, Marvell, Lam Research and Applied Materials each gained more than 4%.
Palo Alto Networks jumped nearly 10% before the bell after raising its annual revenue forecast and agreeing to buy AI start-up Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in an all-stock deal.
Temu owner PDD Holdings gained more than 7% after third-quarter adjusted profit beat Wall Street forecasts. The company spent less on sales and marketing.
In London, the FTSE 100 fell 49.13 points to 10,502.04, hovering just above the 10,500 mark.
12.30 GMT: FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 fall in lunchtime trade
The FTSE 100 slipped to just above 10,500 at lunchtime, while the FTSE 250 gave up its early gains and fell below 24,300.
Babcock International was the biggest gainer, rising 7.03% to 1,043.50p.
JD Sports Fashion was the biggest faller, down 4.16% to 90.40p.
11.00 GMT: Small-cap Round-Up
Shaires Holdings Ltd (AIM:SHR)) says Anthropic's US$83 IPO price is 41% above its entry price.
88 Energy Ltd (AIM:88E, ASX:88E, OTCQB:EEENF) won four South Prudhoe lease bids and signed a binding Kad River East joint venture memorandum with Forte Energy.
Scancell Holdings PLC (AIM:SCLP, OTC:SCNLF) received FDA regenerative medicine advanced therapy designation for its experimental melanoma treatment.
Anglo Asian Mining Plc (LSE:AAZ, OTC:AGXKF) plans to return Gosha and Ordubad to Azerbaijan.
Ilika PLC (AIM:IKA, OTCQX:ILIKF) reported first-half product revenue of £90,000, up from £5,500.
Sovereign Metals Ltd (ASX:SVM, OTCQX:SVMLF, AIM:SVML) confirmed Tim Carstens has taken over as executive chair.
IXICO PLC (LSE:IXI, OTC:PHYOF) upgraded its brain-imaging platform and announced two collaborations.
Emmerson PLC (AIM:EML) shares were temporarily suspended ahead of a potential equity raise.
Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF) hired Worley for preliminary design of a battery materials pilot plant.
10.00 am GMT: Babcock leads Blue Chips
Babcock International led the FTSE 100's biggest risers on Thursday, climbing 7.18% to 1,045p after reporting a 13% increase in underlying operating profit and reaffirming its full-year guidance.
The defence contractor outperformed a weaker London market, with the FTSE 100 slipping 23.64 points, or 0.22%, to 10,527.53.
Safety equipment and environmental technology group Halma followed, advancing 4.34% to 3,554p, while Polar Capital Technology Trust gained 3.36% to 569.5p.
Luxury fashion group Burberry climbed 2.94% to 1,192p, extending gains among selected consumer stocks despite wider concerns about household spending.
Computacenter added 2.47% to 4,724p, while industrial products distributor Diploma rose 2.25% to 7,040p.
The gains highlighted selective buying in defence, technology and industrial shares despite the broader index remaining under pressure.
9.00am GMT: FTSE flat in early trade
The FTSE 100 was little changed on Thursday, gaining 1.47 points, or 0.01%, to 10,553, as stronger defence and technology shares offset weakness among financial stocks.
The FTSE 250 rose 18.86 points, or 0.08%, to 24,383.03, while the FTSE AIM All-Share slipped 0.16%.
Babcock International led blue-chip gainers, jumping 7.59% after reporting a 13% rise in underlying operating profit, while Halma advanced 3.35% and Polar Capital Technology Trust gained 3.27%.
Investec plunged 7.92% as rising costs and weaker UK profitability overshadowed earnings growth, while JD Sports declined 3.35%.
National Grid fell 2.13% and Vodafone lost 1.93%.
Among mid-caps, Ceres Power surged 8.31%, while Close Brothers tumbled 8.84% and Rank Group dropped 4.02%.
8.15am GMT: FTSE attempts recovery
The FTSE 100 was showing signs of a modest recovery after Wednesday's 138.7-point slump to 10,551.17, with an early UK 100 market indicator rising 0.10%, although a confirmed cash-index opening level was unavailable.
Airtel Africa led early gainers, climbing 3.46%, followed by Anglo American, up 2.12%, and Pershing Square Holdings (LSE:PSH), ahead 2.05%.
Diploma gained 1.67%, while Fresnillo advanced 1.68% as mining shares recovered some lost ground.
National Grid fell 2.21% and Vodafone declined 1.84%, with both stocks trading ex-dividend.
B&M European Value Retail slipped 1.60%, JD Sports lost 1.12% and Severn Trent declined 1.04%.
Overnight, Wall Street closed mixed, while Australia's ASX 200 lost 1.04% and Bitcoin traded around $63,600.
7.00am GMT: FTSE 100 eyes modest rebound
The FTSE 100 is heading for a slightly stronger opening on Thursday, with futures up 13.4 points, or 0.13%, at 10,587.0 in the latest available pre-market indication.
London's blue-chip index slumped 138.7 points, or 1.30%, to 10,551.17 on Wednesday, weighed down by mining stocks and concerns over interest rates.
Wall Street closed mixed overnight, with the Dow Jones falling 561 points, or 1.11%, and the S&P 500 slipping 0.23%, while the Nasdaq gained 0.42% despite Nvidia losing 2.9%.
Asian markets were mixed, with Japan's Nikkei advancing while Hong Kong's Hang Seng and mainland Chinese stocks declined.
Australia's ASX 200 extended its losing streak to six sessions, falling 91.4 points, or 1.04%, to 8,730.4, as mining stocks suffered and unemployment rose to 4.9%.
Brent crude traded around US$92 a barrel, gold hovered near US$3,740 an ounce and sterling stood around US$1.314.
Bitcoin traded around US$63,400 in early dealings after sliding nearly 3% in the previous session.
In London, investors will assess results from Sage, Halma, Babcock and Investec, alongside a trading update from JD Sports.
